On The 5 th Of August, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 742 of 2023
 The National Insurance Co. Ltd. Through Its Branch
 Manager

 Kamal S/O Bhanwarlal Next Friend Mother Leela Bai And

 Appearance:

Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the appellant.
 Shri Akhil Godha, learned counsel for the respondent [R  Shri Manoj Sharma, learned counsel for the respondent [
 ORDER
The present appeal has been filed by the appellant/insurance company being aggrieved by the award dated 20.09.2022 passed in claim case No.104/2017 challenging the quantum of compensation.
2. The short facts of the case are that on 28.09.2016, injured/respondent No.1 was going along with his brother as a pillion rider by motorcycle from village- Raamli to Rajaawataa.

When they reached near village-Mandodaa Jod, the respondent No.2 came driving Tata 407 Metadore registration No.MP09-KB-8483 in a rash and negligent manner and without giving any indicator turned the said vehicle towards village-Mandoda because of which the said vehicle dashed into the motorcycle of the respondent No.1 and both the brothers sustained injuries.
The respondent No.1 sustained grievous injuries on his head because of which he lost his mental balance.
A case was registered at crime No.621/2015 at police station-Mohanbadiya for offence under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC for the said NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:22755 2 MA-742-2023 accident.
3. The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act for the injuries sustained by him.

The claims tribunal after considering the evidence on record concluded that the respondent No.1/claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.19,56,360/- for loss of earning capacity and by awarding compensation in other heads a total sum of Rs.27,03,360/- was awarded.

4. The learned counsel for appellant/insurance company challenged the award on the ground that the claims tribunal has erred in considering permanent disability of the respondent no. 1 at 100%,

1 when it was also observed in the impugned award itself that the injured was never treated by a psychiatrist whereas 100% disability has been taken only with respect to mental dis-balance of the respondent No.1.
He further submits that there was no material evidence/documents on record to establish that the respondent No.1 was mentally disturbed.

5. Learned counsel for the insurance company has strongly emphasized towards the fact that the respondent No.1/claimant has himself appeared before the tribunal at the time of registration of the claim case and his appearance continued for the next two years.
It was also pointed out that the injured himself has signed his presence in the proceedings of the case.
He submits that all these circumstances points out towards the fact that the respondent No.1 was not 100% disabled mentally.

Apart from this, it has also been argued by the learned counsel for the appellant that the claims tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the injured at very higher side, thus, he prays for reduction of the amount of compensation.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.1/claimant submits that it has clearly been recorded by the claims tribunal in para 18 of the award that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:22755 3 MA-742-2023 appellant has sustained permanent disability inasmuch as he has lost his mental balance.

He further submits that the assessment of income of the injured is correct at Rs.6850/- per month, which has been taken on the basis of notification issued by the labour commissioner, Indore on 28.09.2016 thereby prescribing minimum wages for unskilled labourer.
As such, he supports the findings of the award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

It is seen from the proceedings of this case that on 10.08.2023 this Court directed for bringing the respondent No.1-Kamal to Indore for assessment and verification of his metal disability by medical board at MY Hospital, Indore.
Pursuant to the said order, report has been submitted by medical board on 18.09.2023.

In the report, it has been mentioned that the respondent No.1-Kamal was examined by medical board on 18.09.2023 the CT Head of relevant time was Suggestive of Left Fronto Temporal Contusion with Minimal Mass effect and Edema.
It is observed in the report that the respondent No.1 obeys simple verbal commands on persistent stimulation and also had some unclear vocalization.
It has also been observed that for further assessment of his current mental status some more tests are needed.
9. From the reading of the aforesaid report, it appears that the respondent No.1-Kamal did suffer permanent disability but not to the extent of 100%.

It appears from the report that though he is able to respondent to commands but to a large extent he is suffering from some mental disability in responding to verbal commands properly and it needed persistence to make him understand the command, report also suggests problems in vocalization.

In this view of the matter, it appears that though the claims tribunal has recorded that the respondent No.1 has suffered 100% permanent disability but the same is not to the extent of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:22755 4 MA-742-2023 100% but it does appears to be grave and concerning.

As regards the income of the respondent No.1, it is seen that the assessment of income is based on the notification issued by the labour commissioner as such no fault can be found with the income as assessed by the labour

sentences.text: In totality of circumstances, this Court is not inclined to requantify the compensation or to remand the case back for reassessment of permanent disability of the respondent No.1.
In the fitness of things, the compensation awarded by the claims tribunal as Rs.27,03,360/- is reduced by a lump-sum amount of Rs.2 Lacs.
It is held that the respondent No.1 is entitled for compensation of an amount of Rs.25,03,360/-.
Rest of the conditions of the award shall remain intact.
The appeal thus stands disposed of in above terms.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
